records.text: and the Lord’s instruction opens my ears. I do not disobey or contradict.
I have given my back to scourges and my cheeks to slaps. I did not turn my face away from the shame of spitting.
The Lord became my helper; therefore I was not abashed. Instead, I set my face like solid rock and knew that I would certainly not be ashamed.
For the One who justified me draws near. Who is bringing a case against me? Let him stand against me together. Who is bringing a case against me? Let him approach me.
Behold, the Lord helps me. Who will harm me? Behold, all of you will grow old like a garment, and it will devour you like a moth.
After Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, behold, magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem,
saying, “Where is the One born King of the Jews? For we saw His star at its rising and have come to bow before Him.”
When King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
He gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people and asked them where the Christ was to be born.
They told him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is what has been written through the prophet:
‘And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd My people Israel.’”
Before the woman in labor gave birth, before the pain of labor came, she escaped and bore a male.
Who heard such a thing, and who has seen anything like it? Did a land labor in one day, or was a nation born all at once? For Zion labored and bore her children.
‘But I gave this expectation, and you did not remember Me,’ said the Lord. ‘Behold, did I not make the woman who gives birth and the barren woman?’ said God.
I will raise up one shepherd over them, My servant David, and he will shepherd them and be their shepherd.
I, the Lord, will be their God, and David a ruler among them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
I will make a covenant of peace with David and remove harmful beasts from the land. They will dwell in the wilderness and sleep in the woods.
Thus says the Lord Sabaoth: “As I said, so it will be, and as I counseled, so it will endure,
to destroy the Assyrians from My land and from My mountains. They will become a trampling place; their yoke will be removed from them, and their glory removed from the shoulders.”
This is the counsel the Lord has counseled concerning the whole inhabited world, and this the high hand over all the world’s nations.
For what the holy God has counseled, who will scatter? And who will turn back the high hand?
I will heal their dwellings; I will love them openly, because My anger turned away from them.
I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like a lily and put down his roots like Lebanon.
His branches will spread, and he will be like an olive tree laden with fruit; his fragrance will be like Lebanon.
I am like turmoil to Ephraim and like a goad to Judah’s house.
Ephraim saw his illness and Judah his pain; Ephraim went to the Assyrians and sent ambassadors to King Jarim. But he could not heal you, and pain will certainly not cease among you.
For I am like a panther to Ephraim and like a lion to Judah’s house. I seize and will go away and take, and there will be no one to rescue.
I will go and return to My place until they disappear; they will seek My face, and in their affliction they will rise early toward Me, saying,
“Judah, may your brothers praise you; your hands shall be upon the backs of your enemies, and your father’s sons shall bow down to you.
“Judah is a lion’s cub. From a shoot, my son, you have gone up. You reclined and slept as a lion, and as a cub; who shall rouse him?
“A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until the things reserved for him come; and he shall be the expectation of nations.
Rejoice greatly, daughter Zion; proclaim, daughter Jerusalem. Behold, your king comes to you, righteous and saving, gentle, and mounted upon a beast of burden and a young colt.

He will destroy chariots from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem; the battle bow will be destroyed, and abundance and peace from the nations. He will rule waters as far as the sea and the earth’s river outlets.

Because even if they offer a sacrifice and eat meat, the Lord will not accept them. Now He will remember their injustices and punish their sins. They returned to Egypt and will eat unclean things among the Assyrians.
Israel forgot his Maker, and they built sacred precincts; Judah multiplied walled cities. I will send fire into his cities, and it will devour their foundations.
And when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not learn to do after the abominations of those nations.
There shall not be found among you one who purifies his son or his daughter by fire, or practises divination, or interprets spoken omens, or observes auguries, or works sorcery,
or chants spells, or is a medium, or observes portents, or inquires of the dead.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination unto the Lord your God; for because of these abominations the Lord shall destroy them from before you.
You shall be perfect before the Lord your God.
For these nations whose possession you inherit hearken unto omens and divinations; but the Lord your God has not granted you so to do.
You shall utterly destroy all the places wherein the nations whose possession you inherit served their gods, upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under the leafy tree.
And you shall pull down their altars, and break their pillars, and cut down their sacred groves, and burn the graven images of their gods with fire; and their name shall perish from that place.
You shall not do so unto the Lord your God,
Draw near, nations, and hear, rulers! Let the earth and those in it hear, the inhabited world and the people in it!
For the Lord’s wrath is against all nations, and anger against their number, to destroy them and hand them over to slaughter.
Their wounded and dead will be thrown out; their odor will rise, and mountains will be soaked with their blood.
Heaven will roll up like a scroll, and all the stars will fall like leaves from a vine, like leaves falling from a fig tree.
